lab06-s000.title: Before you begin this lab
lab06-s000.markdown:
**Estimated time:** 25 minutes
**What you will create in this module:** A report that a CFO can use for everyday decisions. Embed an editable planning sheet in a canvas and display variances from the previous year, KPIs combining multiple measures, and a financial matrix. > [!IMPORTANT] > **Note on data sources:** Input measures in a planning sheet and actuals measures in the semantic model are different values, even when their names are similar. The following steps identify each source explicitly so that you assign the correct values to canvas visuals. ---

lab06-s001.title: Review of the work so far
lab06-s001.markdown:
The content you created in the previous 5 modules is in planning sheets. Planning sheets are useful for people preparing budgets, but can be difficult for executives to interpret as they are.

**Intelligence sheets** are the reporting canvas in Fabric Planning. You create them within the same Plan item and can reference the same semantic model, as well as embed planning sheets directly in the canvas. This last capability is a particular difference from creating a separate Power BI report. When you embed a planning sheet, you can use its measures as inputs to visuals. Visuals assigned sheet input measures from **From Sheets** let you see planning changes on the same canvas. Visuals that reference only the semantic model do not change when you edit the sheet.

> [!NOTE]
> **Model used in this exercise:** Microsoft's intelligence sheets tutorial uses a SaaS sample model with predefined base measures for Actuals, Plan, and Forecast. This exercise uses the Harborlight model. A Plan item is associated with one semantic model, so you can work with the plans created in Modules 01–05 and the canvas using the same model.
>
> The Harborlight model does not have the same *Plan* or *Forecast* base measures as the SaaS sample. In this exercise, retrieve `2026 Sales Plan`, created in Module 02, from **From Sheets → Plan Intro** and compare it with the model's `2025 Gross Revenue`. Select input measures and model actuals from their respective sources.

Continue working in the same `Harborlight_FY26_Plan` item.

---

lab06-s002.title: Step 1: Create an intelligence sheet
lab06-s002.markdown:
1. On the **Home** ribbon, select **New Intelligence Sheet**.
2. Enter `FY26 Plan Review` as the name and select **Create**.

The **Visualizations** pane and canvas open. Unlike a planning sheet, this is a free-form surface where you can position visuals wherever you like.

![Creation dialog with FY26 Plan Review entered as the name](../assets/screenshots/lab06/lab06-03-new-intelligence-name-dialog.png)

![FY26 Plan Review and its empty canvas after creation](../assets/screenshots/lab06/lab06-04-created-empty-canvas.png)

lab06-s003.title: Step 2: Embed the planning sheet first
lab06-s003.markdown:
Complete this step before creating visuals. Until you embed a planning sheet, its measures do not appear in the **Data** pane and cannot be referenced in the following steps.

1. On the **Visualization** tab, select **Planning**.
2. In the sheet selection dialog, select **Select an Existing Planning Sheet**, specify `Plan Intro`, and select **Add**.
3. Resize and reposition the embedded sheet to leave room for visuals alongside it.

![Plan Intro selected with Add enabled](../assets/screenshots/lab06/lab06-06-plan-intro-selected-enabled-add.png)

![Canvas immediately after embedding Plan Intro](../assets/screenshots/lab06/lab06-07-embedded-plan-intro-in-canvas.png)

> [!IMPORTANT]
> If the Plan item contains no planning sheets, **Planning** in the visuals menu is grayed out. If you cannot select it, check that you have opened the correct Plan item.

Next, open the **Data** pane.

Expand **From Sheets** and check that `2026 Target` and `2026 Sales Plan`, created in Module 02, appear under `Plan Intro`. These are input measures created with **Data Input**. They are different values from any model measures with the same names.

![2026 Target and 2026 Sales Plan under Plan Intro in From Sheets](../assets/screenshots/lab06/lab06-08-from-sheets-plan-input-measures.png)

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **If From Sheets is empty:** If you see `No Other Sheets Available`, check that `Plan Intro`, where you created the input columns in Module 02, has been saved and that you embedded a sheet from the same Plan item. You can try basic visual operations using only model actuals measures, but comparisons with the plan require input measures.
>
> Distinguish **From Sheets** data from model data by their source trees, not just their display names. In [Blending measures](https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/iq/plan/infobridge-how-to-blend-measures), too, measures from other sheets are selected from From Sheets.

Changes are reflected in visuals that reference the input measure. It is normal for charts referencing only model baseline values to remain unchanged.

lab06-s004.title: Step 3: Visualize plan versus prior-year actuals
lab06-s004.markdown:
1. In the **Visualizations** pane, select **Charts 100+**.
2. Search for `variance` and select **Integrated variance bar** from the **Bar/ Column** results.
3. Assign fields as follows. **Actual(s)** in the UI is the field well for the primary series. Here, assign the plan values to it. Their business meanings are “FY26 Plan” and “FY25 Actuals.”

   | Field well | Field | Source |
   |---|---|---|
   | **Actual(s)** | *2026 Sales Plan* | **From Sheets → Plan Intro** |
   | **Comparison 1 (vs Actuals)** | *2025 Gross Revenue* | **Measures Table** in the semantic model |
   | **Category** | *Region*, followed by *Category* | Semantic model |

4. Check that the assignment order in **Category** is *Region* → *Category*. Use **Show Next Level** to move to product categories and **Drill Up** to return to regions. Then double-click **Expand Next Level** to display the 5 product categories for each of the 4 regions. If the labels are too small to read, enlarge the visual with **Focus** and return with **Back to Sheet**.
5. Select a data label and choose `Thousands` in the on-object **Datalabel Scaling Dropdown**.
6. Select a bar and set **Series colours**.

![Chart gallery with variance search results](../assets/screenshots/lab06/lab06-15-variance-chart-gallery.png)

![Assignments showing the plan and prior-year actuals sources and Region followed by Category](../assets/screenshots/lab06/lab06-18-variance-region-category-order.png)

![Display after moving to product categories with Show Next Level](../assets/screenshots/lab06/lab06-20-variance-product-level-rendered.png)

![Both levels expanded in Focus to check labels for 4 regions and 5 product categories](../assets/screenshots/lab06/lab06-22-expanded-variance-focus-mode.png)

![Menu for selecting Thousands for data labels](../assets/screenshots/lab06/lab06-24-datalabel-scaling-options.png)

![Labels such as 7,180.5k and 9,885.6k after applying Thousands; the axis unit remains m](../assets/screenshots/lab06/lab06-25-datalabel-thousands-applied.png)

**Thousands** controls the display unit of data labels. The axis unit does not necessarily change to thousands at the same time. Set the series colors and compare values for the same region, product, and period, using “plan − prior-year actuals” as the variance basis.

lab06-s005.title: Step 4: Display trends over time
lab06-s005.markdown:
1. In the **Visualizations** pane, select **Charts 100+**, expand **Line**, and select **Grouped/Clustered Line**.
2. Assign fields as follows. Both **Actual(s)** and **Legend** are required fields marked with an asterisk. Until they are populated, the visual remains a gray placeholder.

   | Field well | Field | Source |
   |---|---|---|
   | **Category** | *Month Short* | **Date** in the semantic model |
   | **Actual(s)** | *2025 Gross Revenue* | **Measures Table** in the semantic model |
   | **Forecast** | *2026 Sales Plan* | **From Sheets → Plan Intro** |
   | **Legend / Color by / Stacked** | *Region* | Semantic model |

Compare monthly prior-year actuals with the FY26 plan. Here, **Forecast** is the visual's field well name, not the `Forecast` measure from Module 04. Name the series “FY25 Actuals” and “FY26 Plan.” Check the January-to-December order and that both series compare the same months and regions.

> [!WARNING]
> **Check the display:** Assigning the plan to **Forecast** does not mean that a plan line has been rendered. If the line is missing, check the field sources, month order, and region assignment. The available series depend on the visual type.

If Grouped/Clustered Line does not display the plan line, try a separate visual, **Variance line**, as an alternative. This does not repair the Forecast assignment in Grouped/Clustered Line.

![Initial Variance line configuration with Category, Actual(s), and Comparison 1; add Region to Trellis Row to complete it](../assets/screenshots/lab06/variance-line-fields.png)

1. In **Visualizations** → **Charts 100+**, search for `variance` and select **Variance line**.
2. Assign the semantic model's *Date → Month Short* to **Category**, **From Sheets → Plan Intro → 2026 Sales Plan** to **Actual(s)**, the model's **Measures Table → 2025 Gross Revenue** to **Comparison 1**, and *Region* to **Trellis Row**.
3. In **Focus**, check the Jan–Dec order for each region and verify that both the plan and actuals series are rendered. If they are not, recheck assignments and sources; do not treat the lines as displayed.

After creating the alternative visual, check both its field assignments and rendered result on screen. The preceding Grouped/Clustered Line images do not demonstrate the configuration or success of Variance line.

![Line chart field assignments for Category, Actual(s), Forecast, and Legend](../assets/screenshots/lab06/lab06-28-line-plan-actual-month-region-assigned.png)

![Line chart in Focus showing months from Jan to Dec and actuals series for 4 regions](../assets/screenshots/lab06/lab06-29-line-focus-month-order-and-series.png)

> [!NOTE]
> The input columns in Module 02 were created by copying FY25 actuals. Do not assume that the original date keys have moved to 2026 just because the column is named `2026 Sales Plan`. Compare in the same date context as the source sheet. For forecasting across actual dates spanning years, use `Forecast` from Module 04. When needed, embed that sheet and verify its location in From Sheets.

lab06-s006.title: Step 5: Create KPIs linked to sheet inputs
lab06-s006.markdown:
1. In the **Visualizations** pane, select **KPIs**. A Card-style KPI is added.
2. Assign fields as follows, **checking their sources**. For the required **Actual(s)** field, select the input measure from From Sheets, not the model measure with the same name.

   | Field well | Field | Source |
   |---|---|---|
   | **Category** | *Region* | Semantic model |
   | **Actual(s)** | *2026 Sales Plan* | **From Sheets → Plan Intro** |
   | **Comparison 1 (vs Actuals)** | *2025 Gross Revenue* | **Measures Table** in the semantic model |
   | **Trellis Row** | *Category* | Semantic model |

   Here, limit the comparison to prior-year actuals. There are 3 comparison field wells, but even when adding targets or forecasts, explicitly identify the sheet or model supplying the values. To add `Forecast` from Module 04, embed its source sheet, verify its location in From Sheets, and then assign it.

![KPI assignments for plan, prior-year actuals, Region, and product Category](../assets/screenshots/lab06/lab06-11-kpi-region-product-trellis-assigned.png)

![Rendered cards for 5 product categories aggregated across all regions; Trellis Column is empty](../assets/screenshots/lab06/lab06-12-kpi-region-trellis-column-added.png)

In the image, **Trellis Column** remains empty. The display shows 5 product categories aggregated across all regions, not 20 region-specific cards.

3. In the current 5-card configuration, KPIs aggregate all regions. Select a leaf-level cell in **2026 Sales Plan** and record its value before editing and the all-region KPI value for the same Category. For a regional comparison, first configure a Region filter or region-specific cards and check that both values have the same region and Category context.
4. Change only one leaf-level cell by a small amount. In the all-region KPI, check that the change to that cell is reflected in the Category total while the comparison value, **2025 Gross Revenue**, remains unchanged. If you added region-specific KPIs, compare values for the same region and Category. If pressing Enter moves the selection, reselect the same leaf-level cell you changed before checking.
5. Restore the original value and check that the KPI also returns to its original value. If aggregation, locks, or filters prevent the expected change from appearing, check the source and target cell. If you cannot edit in the embedded sheet, inspect the visual with **Focus**, then return to the original Planning sheet and edit the same cell.

lab06-s007.title: Step 6: Create a financial matrix
lab06-s007.markdown:
1. In the **Visualizations** pane, select **Matrix**.
2. Assign fields as follows.

   | Field well | Field | Source |
   |---|---|---|
   | **Rows** | *Category*, *Sub Category* | *Product* |
   | **Columns** | *Quarter*, *Month Short* | *Date* in the semantic model |
   | **Values (AC)** | *2026 Sales Plan* | **From Sheets → Plan Intro** |
   | **Compare to Prior Period (PY)** | *2025 Gross Revenue* | *Measures Table* in the semantic model |

3. On the **Matrix** tab, select **Show Columns** and enable **Variance** and **Variance %**.
4. Set the display names to “FY26 Plan” and “FY25 Actuals.” Do not equate the UI labels Actuals and PY directly with their business meanings.
5. For one category, manually check that the variance is **plan − prior-year actuals** and the variance percentage is **(plan − prior-year actuals) ÷ prior-year actuals**. If prior-year actuals are 0, do not treat the variance percentage as 0%. If the screen shows 0 or a blank, distinguish it as a display resulting from an undefined denominator. If the sign or comparison direction is reversed, review field assignments and variance settings.

![Matrix assignments for Rows, Columns, Values (AC), and Compare to Prior Period (PY)](../assets/screenshots/lab06/lab06-33-matrix-plan-actual-rows-columns-assigned.png)

When checking variance display columns and series names, do not confuse the AC/PY assignment order with the displayed column order.

The comparison direction is “plan − prior-year actuals.” Use quarters and months, not years, in the columns to align periods with the plan column created by copying FY25 actuals.

Display variance columns with **Show Columns**. Check variances and variance percentages across multiple quarters and categories, paying attention to how a zero denominator is displayed.

> [!TIP]
> The **Matrix** tab also provides **Templates** → **Financial**. You can apply indentation, subtotals, and bold parent rows together. Try it on a matrix with an account hierarchy.

lab06-s008.title: Step 7: Filter all visuals with one filter
lab06-s008.markdown:
1. In the **Visualizations** pane, select **Super Filter**.
2. Assign **Data → Semantic Model → Date → Year** to the filter's **Category**.
3. Set both the start and end of the numeric range to `2025` and confirm. After processing finishes, reread both input fields and verify `2025 / 2025`.
4. Record each visual's values under the same conditions before narrowing the period, then compare the period and values across all visuals. Finally, restore the original range and check again.

![Year filter positioned at the top with size and position settings](../assets/screenshots/lab06/lab06-38-year-filter-header-layout.png)

If the Date dimension has no actual date field, use the numeric range for **Year**. Setting the start and end to the same year filters to that year.

<details>
<summary>Using the Calendar format</summary>

For a model with an actual date field, you can configure the Calendar format as follows.

1. In the **Visualizations** pane, select **Calendar**.
2. Assign the *Date* dimension to the field well.
3. Select the pencil icon to open **Properties**. Set **Type** to **Date** and the date mode to **Calendar**.
4. Select a date range.

</details>

lab06-s009.title: Step 8: Improve the layout
lab06-s009.markdown:
1. On the **Intelligence** tab, select **Elements** → **Text**.
2. Enter `Harborlight Provisions - FY26 Plan Review`.
3. Increase the font size, make the text bold, and place the text box at the top of the canvas.

Align the canvas elements and set the following sizes and positions as needed.

lab06-s010.title: Canvas and element sizes and positions
lab06-s010.markdown:
1. Set the canvas page settings to **Type = Custom**, **Scaling Unit = Pixel**, **Width = 1600**, and **Height = 1800**.
2. From the **Intelligence** menu, open the menu for managing common properties of elements. Its tooltip is **Manage common properties for all elements, including background, dimensions, and other layout settings.**
3. Select the target element, enter and confirm the following values in **Layout → General → Dimension & Position**, then reread the fields.

| Element | Width | Height | X Position | Y Position |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Year filter | 1580 | 90 | 10 | 80 |
| KPI | 780 | 550 | 10 | 200 |
| Variance bar chart | 780 | 550 | 810 | 200 |
| Embedded Plan Intro | 1580 | 450 | 10 | 1330 |

Set the Year filter's own font size to 14. Adjust element positions to fit your canvas layout.

![Canvas settings showing 1600×1800 in Pixel units](../assets/screenshots/lab06/lab06-14-pixel-unit-custom-1600x1800-applied.png)

![Size and position of the embedded Plan Intro](../assets/screenshots/lab06/lab06-37-embedded-sheet-layout-position-and-size.png)

![KPI size and position](../assets/screenshots/lab06/lab06-39-kpi-layout-pixel-bounds.png)

![Variance bar chart size and position](../assets/screenshots/lab06/lab06-40-variance-bar-layout-pixel-bounds.png)

lab06-s011.title: Save
lab06-s011.markdown:
1. Select **Save**.
2. Wait for saving to finish and check that **Report saved successfully!** appears.

![Save success message](../assets/screenshots/lab06/lab06-43-recovery-checkpoint-save-complete.png)

lab06-s012.title: Step 9: Review with shared numerical context
lab06-s012.markdown:
1. Select a cell or data point in the matrix.
2. On the top ribbon, select **Comments** → **Add new comment**.
3. Enter a comment. If needed, type `@` followed by a colleague's name and select a mention suggestion. Enter may only confirm a suggestion, so do not assume the comment has been posted; select **Send**.
4. Save the Report, reload normally, select the same cell or data point, and check that the comment appears. For mention notifications, distinguish checking the displayed setting from confirming receipt with the recipient.

Comments are tied to the target context and displayed with the current filter state taken into account. Check the available commenting granularity and mention notification behavior in the interface you are using.

---

lab06-s013.title: Check your understanding
lab06-s013.markdown:
1. What are the benefits of embedding a planning sheet in the canvas?
2. How does semantic model data differ from **From Sheets** data?
3. If **From Sheets** is empty, can you say that you have verified the live KPI?

<details>
<summary>Answers</summary>

1. You can edit the plan on the canvas and see changes in KPIs that reference its input measures. Visuals referencing only model values do not change when you edit the plan.
2. Semantic model data consists of actuals and planning baseline values from the connected model. **From Sheets** references values managed in planning sheets, such as Data Input columns, simulations, and formula measures. Even with the same name, values from different sources are different values.
3. No. Check the input columns created in Module 02, the sheet where they were saved, the embedded sheet, and the sources. Change and restore one cell to verify that the KPI is linked to the input measure.

</details>

---
